England.difference_en: England formally connects tenths and hundredths with fractions in Year 4 and extends to thousandths in Year 5. China's third learning stage develops decimal meaning and counting units; exact current textbook placement remains pending.
England.why_en: Decimal place value should remain connected to units such as tenths and hundredths rather than being read as a string of digits.
England.classroom_use_en: Read each decimal as a number of tenths or hundredths as well as with standard decimal notation.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 4 develops tenths and hundredths; Grade 5 extends to thousandths and explicitly develops the ten-times relationship between adjacent places.
US.why_en: Decimals remain part of the base-ten place-value system rather than a separate notation system.
US.classroom_use_en: Compare 0.5 and 0.35 as five tenths and thirty-five hundredths before using a written comparison rule.

England.difference_en: England explicitly connects tenths/hundredths fractions with decimals across Years 4-5.
England.why_en: Fractions and decimals can be different notations for the same quantity.
England.classroom_use_en: Place 1/2, 5/10 and 0.5 at the same point on one number line.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 4 writes fractions with denominators 10 or 100 in decimal notation and compares decimals to hundredths.
US.why_en: Decimal notation grows directly from base-ten fractions.
US.classroom_use_en: Build 0.37 from 37/100 and confirm it with a hundred grid or number line.

England.difference_en: England progressively compares and orders decimals using place value and number lines.
England.why_en: Whole-number rules such as 'more digits means larger' do not apply to decimal magnitude.
England.classroom_use_en: Compare 0.5 and 0.35 by writing 0.50 and identifying the value of each place.

US.difference_en: Common Core compares decimals to hundredths in Grade 4 and to thousandths in Grade 5, requiring comparisons to be based on digit values.
US.why_en: The comparison is made place by place, not by treating the decimal digits as a whole number.
US.classroom_use_en: After the answer, ask which place was compared first and why.

England.difference_en: England connects decimal addition/subtraction and later multiplication/division to the place-value structure of whole-number methods.
England.why_en: The structure of the algorithm can transfer, but place values and units must remain aligned.
England.classroom_use_en: Label ones, tenths and hundredths before using a written method rather than only saying 'line up the decimal points'.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 5 uses place value and operation properties for decimal operations and connects strategies with written methods.
US.why_en: Place-value reasoning explains decimal placement and the magnitude of partial products or quotients.
US.classroom_use_en: Estimate the result first and use the estimate to check the decimal point in the final answer.

England.difference_en: England Year 5 defines percent as parts per hundred and connects percentages with fractions over 100 and decimals. China's 2022 standard places percentage in Statistics and Probability in the third learning stage and emphasises contextual/statistical meaning.
England.why_en: Both use 'per 100' meaning, but the Chinese standard gives percentage a more explicit data-description role.
England.classroom_use_en: Use class survey data as well as discount questions, and always identify the whole to which the percentage refers.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 6 develops percent as a rate per 100 within Ratio and Proportional Relationships.
US.why_en: This places percent directly alongside ratio, unit rate and unknown-quantity problems.
US.classroom_use_en: For every percentage, ask '50% of what whole?' before calculating.

England.difference_en: England Years 5-6 explicitly connect common fractions, decimals and percentages as equivalent forms.
England.why_en: The forms are useful in different contexts while representing the same quantity.
England.classroom_use_en: For common equivalences, require at least one model or number-line justification rather than only a conversion table.

US.difference_en: Common Core builds fraction-decimal connections in Grades 4-5 and introduces percent in Grade 6; it is not organised as one single three-way conversion standard.
US.why_en: The progression moves from base-ten fractions to decimals and later into ratio/percent reasoning.
US.classroom_use_en: Ask why 0.25, 1/4 and 25% represent the same quantity rather than only converting mechanically.
